messages:
anna: Quick heads-up — our FP8 canary showed ~0.8% perplexity shift vs float baseline on the small eval set, but rerun with a fixed seed looks better. wonder how much of this is true model degradation vs nondeterministic kernels?
liam: Could be both. on Ampere/Turing there are nondet kernels (atomic adds, kernel fusion) that change fp8 rounding. also cudnn has nondet algo choices unless you force deterministic.
sara: Repro tip: are we fixing torch/cuda seeds and forcing single-threaded CPU? I saw variability from CPU multithread interleaving too.
anna: yes I reran with torch.manual_seed(42) + torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True) — that tightened numbers but didn’t fully close gap.
liam: If you use deterministic_algorithms it might switch to slower fallback kernels. tradeoff: reproducible vs perf. for an eval harness that's fine, but prod serving can't afford it.
mike: From infra side we should capture kernel/driver/compiler metadata in the quant profile snapshot. CUDA version, cuDNN version, kernel flags, and whether stochastic rounding was enabled. otherwise we lose the mapping between profile and observed quality.
sara: Agreed. Also: add a "deterministic": "yes/no/soft" field in the quant profile metadata. "soft" means best-effort determinism (no perf-killing fallbacks). That gives ops teams a clear signal.
anna: +1. Another operational question: should calibration code include multiple seeds and report median/iqr? single-seed calibration hides worst-case drift.
liam: We already have a multi-seed calibration mode in the prototype — runs N seeds and aggregates. idea: surface both mean and 90th quantile degradation metrics in the profile.
mike: For serialization: profile schema needs a version and a checksum. If a profile was generated on cudnn 8.3 vs 8.4 we should mark it incompatible unless validated. Rolling back a driver could silently change outputs.
sara: For the eval harness, let's add a short smoke test that runs a deterministic path (single seed, deterministic kernels) and a production-like path (fast kernels, default flags) and compare deltas. If delta > threshold, flag the profile.
anna: Can we also log runtime counters about which kernels were used during the profiling run? that helps reproduce by forcing the same kernel selections later.
liam: We can — runtime can emit kernel IDs and a small fingerprint. but note kernel selection is influenced by sequence length and batch shape; include those inputs in the profile snapshot.
mike: Ops note: storing kernel ids + driver versions increases profile size. propose we store a lightweight fingerprint (hash of kernel ids + cuda/cuDNN versions) and an optional full blob for debugging.
sara: QA checklist proposal: 1) multi-seed calibration, 2) deterministic vs production smear test, 3) kernel fingerprint present, 4) profile schema version >= X, 5) regression metrics (mean, p90).
anna: I'll open a short RFC follow-up with the proposed profile fields and QA checklist. keeping this thread as a quick sync. thanks all :thumbsup:
calib-bot: [calibration-run] profile 0x7f3a saved (seed-median: 0.12% deg, seed-p90: 0.45%). artifacts: s3://redwood/quant-profiles/1768800123-0x7f3a.tar.gz
liam: Nice — that payload should include kernel-fingerprint and seed-trace. can we add a human-readable summary to the S3 manifest? helps oncall triage.
mike: we'll add manifest metadata. also: ops will index profile checksums so we can detect identical profiles across customers.
sara: final operational ask: when a profile is marked "soft deterministic" we should expose an alert if a production rollout sees a delta > configured tolerance. automated rollback if SLA-sensitive route.
anna: noted. RFC follow-up will include rollout guard behavior.
